item.title: Industry 5.0-driven Product Lifecycle Management: toward human-centric, sustainable, and resilient manufacturing
item.content:encoded:
Romeo Bandinelli, University of Florence

Monica Rossi, Politecnico di Milano

Claudio Sassanelli, Politecnico di Bari

Virginia Fani, Universitas Mercatorum

This special issue addresses how Product Lifecycle Management systems must evolve to support Industry 5.0's three foundational principles: human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience. Traditional PLM systems, designed primarily for data integration and process efficiency, lack mechanisms to support operator well-being, embed circular economy strategies, ensure regulatory compliance, or enable rapid adaptation during disruptions.

The special issue introduces PLM 5.0 as a strategic governance platform that integrates lifecycle data, human interaction, sustainability metrics, and adaptive decision-making across industrial ecosystems. It seeks conceptual, empirical, methodological, and case-based contributions that explore how PLM systems should be redesigned, how organizations can integrate circular economy principles, what governance frameworks are needed, and how manufacturing can build resilience through lifecycle management.

Appel publié par Journal of Manufacturing Technology Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Redesigning PLM Systems for Industry 5.0
  • Human-Centric PLM and Operator Development
  • Circular Economy Integration within PLM
  • Sustainable Lifecycle Assessment and Net-Zero Strategies
  • Resilient Manufacturing and Adaptive Lifecycle Management
  • Governance, Interoperability, and Data Management Frameworks
  • Decision-Support and Managerial Transformation
  • Sector-Specific Applications with Cross-Industry Implications

Timeline

  • May 6, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • October 31, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
item.content:encoded:
Ruoqi Geng, Cardiff University

Di Li, University of Warwick

Yang Cheng, Aalborg University

This special issue seeks empirical research demonstrating how artificial intelligence is embedded within and enhances digital production technologies in real operational contexts. The focus is on understanding implementation pipelines and socio-technical conditions that enable AI-enabled solutions to function effectively as operational workflows. Purely conceptual, literature-based, or modelling studies without empirical validation are excluded.

Acceptable empirical research uses real-world operational evidence such as production logs, IoT sensors, machine telemetry, or industrial case studies, potentially employing machine learning or optimization when grounded in real data and validated in industrial settings with measurable outcomes. Studies must address the full AI implementation pipeline, from translating production decisions into AI use cases, to ensuring data readiness, to embedding AI outputs into human-AI workflows linked to measurable production outcomes.

Appel publié par Production Planning & Control. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI-Augmented Production Planning and Control
  • Business–AI Alignment and AI Readiness Pipeline for Production Systems
  • AI-enabled Quality and Process Control
  • Agentic and Workflow-Oriented Deployment in Production
  • AI-Enabled Cyber–Physical Production Systems and Digital Twins
  • AI and Additive Manufacturing
  • AI and Blockchain for Production Systems
  • Human–AI Interaction and Organisational Transformation
  • Empirical Innovations in Data, Measurement, and Evaluation
  • Extended Production Contexts (Production-Adjacent Physical Operations)

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Call for Papers released
  • June 30, 2027: Manuscript submission deadline
  • September 1, 2027: First-round decisions
  • December 1, 2027: Revised manuscripts due
  • June 1, 2028: Final decisions
